meta.title: Bengali C1 Advanced
meta.subtitle: 622 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Bengali → English (see the Bengali, recall the meaning) and English → Bengali (see an English meaning, recall the Bengali). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 622 words for an advanced learner, aligned to C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognise implicit meaning' — a learner here is able to express themselves fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions, to use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes, and to produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. This level is smaller than the 1,500 words first planned for it, on purpose. By this point the subtitle frequency list has no more everyday words that the levels below have not taught, and most of what the dictionary has left is plant names, regional dialect and archaic literary words; those were left out rather than used to reach the number. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for learners of Bengali, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 287 of the 622 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — scholarship and the study of language and mind, the state, the law and public life, ideas and political movements, administration, society and the workplace, character and judgement, argument and degree, the land, the weather and the measure of the world, health and the body, feeling, everyday things, and the formal register of written Bengali — and the other 335 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Bengali, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. The deck teaches the standard colloquial language (cholito bhasha) shared by West Bengal and Bangladesh; where an everyday word differs between the two — জল and পানি for water, নমস্কার and সালাম for a greeting — both are taught. Every headword is printed in the Bengali script with a romanisation beneath it, Wiktionary's own (ô for the open o of the inherent vowel, ō where the o-sign is written, a dot under the retroflex letters, ẏ and ẇ for the glides: kôra, bhalō), so the deck can be studied before the script is fluent; the Bengali Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script itself. Bengali has no grammatical gender. The 482 nouns show their definite form ('the …', with -টা), their plural and their genitive ('of …'); the 8 verbs show their present, their past and their 'having done' form, where the stem's vowel changes and the irregular verbs show, and behind the All forms fold every tense by person, at the three levels of address — তুই intimate, তুমি familiar, আপনি polite. Real example sentences come with 33 of the 622 words, three apiece for 4 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, forms and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
